constraint_decided_it: The v7.3.2 P144 declaration reads 'Properties: P144.1 kind of member: E55 Type' with FOL P144(x,y,z) ⇒ [P144(x,y) ∧ E55(z)] (and P107 likewise carries P107.1 with P107(x,y,z) ⇒ [P107(x,y) ∧ E55(z)]). B rejects P107.1/P144.1 on the claim that it 'does not appear in the current v7.3.2 property list via docs search' — false, and contradicted by t1806, the very thread B cites, where Doerr treats P144.1 as a live construct. A's defect is narrower: it attributes Christian-Emil's 'There is no separate class and properties for giving somebody a right (privilege)... is not a shortcut' to t1022 (Passive Activities — Sanderson/Beretta/Bruseker, no Christian-Emil message); the wording is verbatim correct but sits in t1019, which A also cites.
better_modelling: The shared modelling both reach is what CRMbase prescribes and I could not beat it: 'Fire-Keeper of [village]' as a singleton E74 Group (scope note: 'official positions ... such as the president of a country', 'the group never had more than one member'), each succession as an E86 Leaving (P145/P146) plus an E85 Joining (P143/P144) — E85's scope note names 'the inauguration of somebody into an official position' and E86's names 'the end of tenure of somebody in an official position' and exemplifies 'George Washington's leaving office in 1797 (E86) separated from the office of President of the United States (E74)'. Domains/ranges all hold: P143 E85→E39, P144 E85→E74, P145 E86→E39, P146 E86→E74. E30 is correctly excluded ('legal privileges'; P105's domain is E72 Legal Object), as is E8 ('does not, however, imply changes of any other kinds of rights'). One refinement neither reached: for the undated handover, give the paired E86 and E85 a single shared E52 Time-Span rather than one each — E52's scope note states 'When used as a common E52 Time-Span for two events, it will nevertheless describe them as being simultaneous, even if nothing else is known', which is exactly what the project's 'unbroken chain' needs when no date is recoverable. B explicitly does the weaker thing ('each gets its own E52 Time-Span'). P107.1 kind of member is legitimate but redundant once the Group *is* the office — A says so; that was the substance of the t0431 negative vote, which did not carry.
reasoning: Both answers land on the same, correct CRMbase modelling with every property inside its declared domain and range, and both correctly redirect away from E30 (E30 is 'legal privileges'; a customary right to light a fire is not one) and from E8 (scope note excludes 'changes of any other kinds of rights'); informality is handled by E52's admitted 'unknown beginning, end and duration' plus P81/P82 bounds, and by P12 being optional. They separate on the accuracy of their support, not their conclusion: B asserts a false fact about the current standard (P107.1/P144.1 absent from v7.3.2) and uses it to discard a declared construct, while contradicting its own cited t1806; A reproduces a real archive sentence but pins it on t1022, which does not contain it. A's E30 rejection is also the better-evidenced one — t0507 (2010, 'can a right be sold or acquired?' — 'here my view has not been so successful'), t1019 and the never-adopted Right Holding proposal in t0976 all check out. B's compensating catches (E8's exclusion, the 1754 club-election fuzzy-date precedent in t0873, oral tradition in the Objectives section) are all verified and real, which keeps the margin slight rather than clear.
